cards.description: Serena Zena is an emerging artist and curator based in Canada. Her multidisciplinary practice delves into the lived experiences and cultural narratives of the Asian diaspora in Canada. Central to her work are themes of identity, intergenerational relationships, and Asian futurism. Her practice blends storytelling with both traditional and emergent media ranging from textiles to extended-reality.

cards.description: Haoran Chang is a Chinese-Canadian artist and designer based in Toronto, Canada. His work explores the intersection of technology, culture, and identity, often through the lens of traditional Chinese art forms. He is particularly interested in how digital media can be used to preserve and reinterpret cultural heritage.

cards.description: Carmela Laganse is an artist and Associate Professor in the School of the Arts at McMaster University. Laganse’s practice engages with intersections of embodied experience and perception as well as exploring the agency embedded in objects and environments. Her work explores the impact of colonialism, diasporic communities and considers how these things contribute to material culture and identity. Working in a variety of media, she often builds interactive work or portable, modular environments that playfully and critically integrate physical, emotional, ritualistic, and intellectual processes through an intersectional lens.

cards.description: Arturo Jimenez is a Hamilton-based Artist and filmmaker. Since 2020, he has been an arts and culture professional working with various artists, artistic organizations, and social service providers in the not-for-profit sector. Arturo’s brand of alternative pop was born from his father’s record collection of the 80s and 90s with a healthy dose of tumblr-era teenaged angst. His work has been featured by CFMU’s Hamiltopia radio block, 100% Electronica’s Stream, and various independent record labels such as First Class Collective, Pacific Plaza, and Virtual Beach Club to name a few! His visual work has been exhibited in McMaster University’s SUMMA Charity Art Auction (2019 & 2020), Centre[3] “In The Off Hours” and at the moma dada gallery.
